subject: Postmortem: Bay Area Developer Summit - attribution & ROI
thread_summary: Post-event ROI and attribution dispute after Bay Area Developer Summit. Sales claims credit for several deals; marketing defends mult-touch methodology. RevOps ran numbers and proposed adjusted crediting and ROI. Final answer: action items for standardized attribution rules and ops deliverables.
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Postmortem: Bay Area Developer Summit - initial rollup

Team —

Attached is the initial KPI rollup from the Bay Area Developer Summit (see BADS_survey_responses.csv). High level: 420 total leads captured, 38 MQLs, 14 SALs handed to sales. Event line item cost (sponsorship + booth + travel + swag + meals): $85,000.

Per the marketing attribution model I applied (multi-touch weighted: first 20%, event 50%, demo 30%), the event influence on pipeline shows ~$420k of influenced pipeline and estimated influenced revenue of ~$210k. I flagged the HubSpot records used in the rollup in the attached list.

We already have a few follow-ups from sales claiming direct pipeline credit — Rafael raised concerns on the last call. I want us to reconcile before the exec summary on Friday. Please review the rollup and answer these questions by EOD Wednesday:
- Sales: which of the 7 deals you flagged do you believe should receive 100% event credit vs partial credit? Include HubSpot IDs.
- RevOps (David): can you run last-touch vs our weighted multi-touch for the 14 SALs and return an adjusted table?
- Marketing (Marissa, Monica): confirm how you applied the weights and any manual adjustments (e.g., known direct-demo conversions).

Attachments: BADS_survey_responses.csv

Thanks —
Lauren
VP, Field Marketing
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Postmortem: Bay Area Developer Summit - initial rollup

Lauren —

Quick note from Sales: we disagree with the way marketing applied event credit on at least 5 of the 7 deals we've surfaced. For example, deal HB-2025-1134 (BrightBridge) was a direct result of a demo request that Erin submitted onsite after our AE followed up on a badge-scan conversation. The prospect explicitly referenced the on-site conversation in the demo request, and the AE logged pipeline same day. We should assign primary credit to the field motion (sales follow-up) but mark event as a significant touch.

I attached a plain list of HubSpot Deal IDs and short notes (HubSpot-deal-IDs.txt). My ask: please mark these 5 as at least 40% credit to Sales for pay/process and reconcile commissions accordingly. If we go full multi-touch as-is, quotas/comp get impacted retroactively.

Short and actionable: can RevOps provide a deal-level breakdown showing who should get credit under last-touch, first-touch, and our weighted model?

—Rafael
Account Executive, West
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Postmortem: Bay Area Developer Summit - initial rollup

Rafael —

Thanks for calling this out. I want to be explicit about how marketing calculated the rollup so we have a shared baseline before RevOps runs alternate models. Methodology recap (attached event_attribution_playbook.pdf):
- We treat the event as an owned channel and apply a weighted multi-touch model for event leads: event touch = 50%, first inbound touch = 20%, demo/AE conversion touch = 30%.
- Manual overrides are used only when the AE emails a prospect and explicitly states the event did not influence the conversion.
- For HB-2025-1134 I see activity: badge scan (event), demo request same day, and multiple subsequent inbound touches. Under our model that still results in ~35–45% event credit depending on exact timestamps. If Sales has marked the AE outreach as the primary origin in HubSpot, we can take that into account, but we need a documented HubSpot field update.

Proposal: David, can you run both: last-touch and our weighted model, then produce a reconciled sheet with recommended % credit per deal and the impact on marketing-sourced pipeline vs sales-sourced pipeline? Let's include explicit timestamp checks for any demo requests happening within 48 hours of the event — those are high-correlation cases.

I also recommend we standardize an "Event Influence" field on the contact record so AEs can flag onsite conversions immediately (checkbox + note). This will reduce noise on retrospective attribution.

Attachments: event_attribution_playbook.pdf

-Marissa
Director, Field Marketing
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Nov 2025 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Postmortem: Bay Area Developer Summit - initial rollup (revops reconciliation)

Team —

Attached is the RevOps reconciliation (roi_rollup_q4_event.csv). I ran three models for the 14 SALs: last-touch, first-touch, and Redwood weighted multi-touch (50% event / 20% first / 30% demo). Key findings:
- Under last-touch, 3 deals (HB-2025-1111, HB-2025-1129, HB-2025-1134) attribute 100% to Sales outreach within 24 hours of a demo.
- Under weighted multi-touch, those same deals still show significant event influence (30–45%), but Sales receives partial credit.
- Adjusted pipeline split (using weighted model with rounding to nearest 5%): Marketing-influenced pipeline = $420,000; Sales-sourced pipeline = $310,000; Total influenced pipeline = $730,000.

Cost / ROI calc per marketing request:
- Event cost: $85,000
- Marketing-influenced pipeline: $420,000
- Estimated influenced revenue (apply conversion 50%): $210,000
- Simple ROI (influenced revenue - cost) / cost = ($210,000 - $85,000) / $85,000 = 1.47 (147%)

Proposal for resolution:
1) Apply weighted multi-touch for external reporting and marketing KPIs.
2) For commissions/hard quota credit, use last-touch for this quarter but implement a transition: starting Q1, switch AE comp to include a 20% credit for event influence (to be finalized by compensation team).
3) Implement the "Event Influence" HubSpot field Marissa suggested; RevOps will own the field and the data pipeline.

I can prep a short appendix for Friday's exec summary that shows both the last-touch and weighted numbers side-by-side. Let me know if you want more granularity by AE or by region.

Attachments: roi_rollup_q4_event.csv

-David
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Postmortem: Bay Area Developer Summit - final notes & action items

Thanks all — quick final recap and retro notes (attached post_event_retro_notes.md):

Summary: RevOps ran the reconciliation and confirmed marketing influenced $420k of pipeline under the weighted model; last-touch assigns 3 deals fully to Sales. Given the impact on commissions, we will:
- Use weighted multi-touch for marketing performance reporting (KPI rollups shown to execs).
- Use last-touch for immediate commission calculations this quarter to avoid retroactive pay changes; update comp plan to incorporate event influence starting Q1.
- RevOps to create the "Event Influence" HubSpot field and backfill the dataset for the last 6 months by Dec 1.
- Field Marketing to add an on-site AE play: checkbox + short script for badge scans + demo scheduling to capture immediate attribution signals.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- David: HubSpot field + backfill (due 2025-12-01)
- Marissa: badge-scan AE script + playbook update (due 2025-11-20)
- Rafael / Sales leadership: confirm commission transition details with comp team (by 2025-11-21)
- Lauren: include appendix comparing last-touch vs weighted in Friday exec note (done)

Thanks again for turning this around quickly. We have a clear path to reconcile pipeline attribution while protecting reps' comp this quarter. Follow-up meeting scheduled if needed.

Attachments: post_event_retro_notes.md

-Lauren
VP, Field Marketing
Redwood Inference
